newsitem.title: TAIWAN: President invests further $69 mln in China.
newsitem.headline: President invests further $69 mln in China.

text.p: Taiwan's food giant President Enterprises Corp, the island's top investor in China, said its shareholders' meeting on Friday approved plans to invest US$69.2 million more in mainland China.

The meeting also authorised the company's board to expand President's investment scale in China in gradual steps, as long as annual investment did not to exceed US$100 million, the firm said in a statement.
Shareholders agreed to issue a 1996 stock dividend of T$2 per share or a bonus issue of 200 shares for every 1,000 shares held, President said.

The meeting approved four investment projects in China worth a total US$69.2 million, including a US$30 million plan to set up an investment holding company that would serve as President's headquarters in the mainland.
The firm would also invest US$22.2 million in a US$74 million joint venture to make beer.
President also planned to invest US$12 million in a hypermarket project, accounting for 45 percent of the joint venture, in Chongqing in the southwestern Sichuan province.
President also would pour US$5 million more into its existing food plant in the northeastern Shenyang city, the statement said.
President currently has some US$900 million invested in various projects in China.

Although Taipei requires all China investments to be routed indirectly through a third place to comply with a ban on direct ties, it remains concerned that its economy may become too dependent on China -- and hence politically vulnerable.
Taipei has banned direct official contact with China since the end of a civil war in 1949 that left the mainland in communist control and Taiwan in the hands of the defeated Nationalists.
Despite Taiwan's ban on direct investment, indirect commerce across the Taiwan strait has flourished since a political thaw began in the late 1980s.
Some 30,000 Taiwan businesses have invested more than US$30 billion in China.
Taipei said in late May it would ban investment in mainland infrastructure -- specifically water works, railways, harbours, airports and power plants.
